prompts.localSystem: You are Guardian, a calm on-device safety assistant. Write a short, reassuring alert for an older adult. Output only JSON {title, text}. No links, no emojis.
prompts.cloudSystem: You are Guardian's cloud assistant. Write a concise, empathetic alert grounded only in the given incident and message. Output only JSON {title, text, sources}. Never invent facts or URLs.

incidents.title: Possible family-emergency scam
incidents.description: A relative in trouble asks for urgent money and says not to call.
incidents.explanation: Scammers impersonate a relative in an emergency so you act before you can verify.
remediation: Call your relative on the number you already have.
Don't send money or gift cards from this chat.
Ask another family member to confirm.

level0.title: Possible scam detected
level0.text: This message asks for urgent money and says not to call. That's a common family-emergency scam. Call your relative on a number you already know.

incidents.title: Unverified alarming news
incidents.description: Big, alarming news with a weak or no source, urging you to share it.
keywords: they don't want you to know
incidents.explanation: Unverified viral claims spread through emotion and urgency; a real story names a credible source.
remediation: Check a trusted news outlet before believing or sharing.
Don't forward it until it is confirmed.

level0.title: Unverified breaking-news claim
level0.text: This post makes an alarming claim without a credible source. Check a trusted news outlet before believing or sharing it.

level2.instruction: Given the claim, search reputable outlets and state whether it is supported, unresolved, or contradicted, citing sources. Keep it short and non-alarmist.

incidents.title: Possible impersonation or payment threat
incidents.description: A fake bank, police or tax office pressures you to verify or pay now.
incidents.explanation: Real banks, authorities and utilities never ask you to verify or pay through a message, and never demand gift cards or crypto.
remediation: Contact the organisation using the number on your card, bill or official app.
Don't tap the link, enter details, or pay by gift card or crypto.
Report the message.

level0.title: Possible impersonation
level0.text: Your bank or the authorities never ask you to 'verify' or pay through a message, and never demand gift cards or crypto. Contact them using the official number.

incidents.title: Possible parcel scam
incidents.description: A held-parcel message asks for a small fee or your details via a link.
incidents.explanation: Couriers do not charge surprise fees through links; the link harvests card details.
remediation: Track the parcel in the courier's official app.
Don't pay through the link.

level0.title: Possible parcel scam
level0.text: A real delivery service won't charge an unexpected fee through a link. Track your parcel in the courier's official app.

incidents.title: Never share this code
incidents.description: Someone asks you to read out or forward a one-time code.
incidents.explanation: A one-time code is the last step to log in or move money; whoever gets it can act as you.
remediation: Never share the code with anyone.
Hang up and contact the bank using the official number.

level0.title: Never share this code
level0.text: No bank or service will ever ask you to read out or forward a code. Don't share it, even if the caller sounds official.

incidents.title: Possible investment scam
incidents.description: Promises guaranteed high returns and pushes you off-platform.
incidents.explanation: Guaranteed high returns do not exist; the platform is fake and early 'profits' are other victims' money.
remediation: Don't send money.
Check whether the firm is licensed with a regulator.
Talk to someone you trust.

level0.title: Possible investment scam
level0.text: 'Guaranteed' high returns are the hallmark of an investment scam. Never send money to an offer pushed through a chat app.

level1.instruction: Explain why 'guaranteed returns' plus off-platform pressure indicate fraud, referencing the specific phrase in the user's message. Give one clear next step.

incidents.title: Blackmail threat
incidents.description: Threatens to expose private images or information unless you pay.
incidents.explanation: Sextortion threats are often bluffs sent in bulk; paying rarely stops them.
remediation: Don't pay.
Keep the messages as evidence.
Block the sender and report it.

level0.title: Blackmail threat
level0.text: This is a common sextortion or blackmail tactic. Do not pay. Keep the messages, block the sender, and report it.

incidents.title: Abusive message
incidents.description: A hostile or abusive message that insults you, including telling you to harm yourself.
incidents.explanation: Abusive messages are meant to hurt. You don't have to engage — but if it touches on self-harm, please reach out to someone you trust or a support service.
remediation: Don't reply.
Block and report the sender.
If it mentions self-harm, talk to someone you trust or contact a local support service.
sources: Guidance — online abuse and self-harm support

level0.title: Abusive message
level0.text: This message is abusive. You don't have to engage — block and report the sender. If it touches on self-harm, please reach out to someone you trust or a local support service.
